title: Build Types, Product Flavours, and the Variant Matrix Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies build types, product flavours, and the variant matrix?
options: Use dimensions for real build-time product differences and explicitly prune unsupported cross-products.
Store production credentials in a flavour
Treat fallbacks as name aliases only
Create a flavour per runtime experiment
questions.answer: Use dimensions for real build-time product differences and explicitly prune unsupported cross-products.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: Every flavour/build-type cross-product must be built and distributed.
questions.explanation: Adding a flavour for every feature flag multiplies variants, source sets and CI cost even when runtime configuration would model the capability safely.

questions.answer: A consumer may receive a different producer variant whose behaviour or dependencies are not semantically compatible.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
